rationale: The read-index receipt (CheckRun d7a20d42d5b84569a0c6e4924cd577a9) resolved all four comparisons, so the completion half of that behaviour is now execution-backed rather than read-only: the request is queued with no read state while the leader has no commit in its term (index 48), the follower acknowledgement moves the leader's commit to 11 (index 49), and the released read state carries read index 11 with the request context that was issued (index 50, both comparisons). I record the observation, state the account at the question level as explained-with-evidence and defect-free, and note the harness correction that unblocked it, since the same deficiency explains the unexplained commit value in an earlier receipt which no conclusion depended on.

knowledge.statement: A leader elected with its append acknowledgement withheld has no commit in its own term, and a ReadIndex request issued then is accepted without producing any read state; once the follower receives that append and its acknowledgement is returned, the leader's commit advances to that index (with matches {1:11, 3:11} out of voters {1,2,3}) and the queued request is released as a read state carrying the index reached at release time and the original request context.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 48, 49 and 50 of CheckRun d7a20d42d5b84569a0c6e4924cd577a9; config ElectionTick=10, HeartbeatTick=1, CheckQuorum+PreVote, ReadOnlySafe, voters {1,2,3} from equal storage snapshots at index=10/term=1, with node 2 never contacted so the quorum is exactly the leader plus node 3; the harness delivery helper writes each Ready's HardState and Entries to that node's MemoryStorage before Advance, which is the application duty the Ready contract states and without which this path cannot complete.

interpretations.rationale: The question is answered, and the answered half is now measured rather than only read. With the leader elected but nothing committed in its term, the ReadIndex request produces no read state at all (index 48), which is the queueing behaviour the sources predicted; the follower's acknowledgement of that term's entry then moves the leader's commit index to 11 with a quorum of matches (index 49); and the released read state carries read index 11 together with the exact request context that was issued (index 50 for both the index and the identity comparison), so the answer is attributable to that request and is at least as new as the moment it was accepted. The remaining half of the question - a request queued by a leader that then loses leadership before committing - stays source-based: nothing clears the queue on a term change and the release helper is reachable only from a leader path, so such a request is answered only if the same node leads again and commits, and otherwise is never answered, which the interface documentation permits by telling callers that read requests can be lost and retries are their job. Nothing here is a defect, and the finding that matters for the main account is unchanged.
counterevidence: The unanswered case is permitted by the same snapshot's ReadIndex documentation, so it cannot be scored as a defect without importing a stronger requirement than the module states.
The answered case is safe rather than merely successful: the released index is the commit index at release time, which is at least as new as the index recorded when the request was accepted.
limitations: The measurement covers the completing path only (queue then release on a commit in the same term); the leadership-loss path that leaves a request unanswered was not exercised in this run and stays source-explained.

Harness correction worth carrying forward: two earlier probes of this run left the leader unable to read its own entries back because the delivery helper never wrote Ready entries to storage, so their commit values stayed at the earlier snapshot index. That deficiency was harness-side, the affected receipts never depended on those values for any comparison, and this receipt uses the corrected helper.
Single process with hand-delivered messages and one configuration; no wall-clock or multi-host behaviour is measured.
